title: Top FBR POS System for Retailers: Expert Comparison
metaDescription: A clear overview of the FBR POS system for retailers in Pakistan — what it is, who must comply, how it works, and what it takes to get and stay compliant.
content:
The overview every retailer needs

If you run a retail business in Pakistan and you are not yet familiar with the FBR POS system, this is the short version of everything that matters. An FBR POS reports each sale to the Federal Board of Revenue in real time and prints a QR-coded invoice the customer can verify. For Tier-1 retailers it is mandatory, and the cost of ignoring it — penalties from PKR 10,000 upward — far outweighs the modest effort of getting set up.

Who has to comply

The obligation falls on Tier-1 retailers: larger shops, chains, and businesses above the FBR turnover threshold. The practical rule of thumb is that if you hold an STRN and trade at any real scale, you should assume integration is required or soon will be.

How it works, briefly

At each sale, your POS submits the invoice to FBR IRIS, IRIS returns a reference, and the POS prints a receipt carrying a QR code that encodes it. Anyone can scan the QR to confirm the sale was reported. The key thing to understand is that the printed receipt is not the proof — the IRIS record is.

Getting compliant

  1. Confirm your STRN is active on IRIS.
  2. Choose a verified IRIS-integrated POS.
  3. Register your terminals and obtain API credentials.
  4. Map products to correct tax rates.
  5. Test invoices and confirm they appear in IRIS.

Staying compliant

The ongoing job is light: reconcile your POS against the IRIS dashboard monthly, keep the software current, and register any new counter or branch. A retail POS also doubles as live inventory, so compliance brings an operational bonus.

faqs.question: What is an FBR POS system for a retailer?
faqs.answer: Software that reports every retail sale to FBR IRIS in real time and issues a QR-coded invoice. It connects your till to FBR so each transaction is recorded as it happens.

faqs.question: Which retailers must comply?
faqs.answer: Tier-1 retailers — broadly larger shops, chains, and businesses above the FBR turnover threshold. If you hold an STRN and trade at scale, integration applies to you.

faqs.question: Is it hard to get started?
faqs.answer: No. A single-shop setup — STRN check, IRIS registration, integration, tax mapping, brief training — is usually complete within a day or two and runs on a phone, tablet, or laptop.

faqs.question: What does staying compliant involve?
faqs.answer: Mainly a monthly reconciliation against the IRIS dashboard and keeping the software updated. The day-to-day reporting is automatic.
